name: 3D Medical Coarse-to-Fine ROI Segmentation Pipeline Template
summary: Reusable base CDG for 3D medical segmentation, RSNA pancreatic cancer detection, contrast-enhanced CT tumor segmentation, organ-and-lesion mask prediction, and coarse-to-fine ROI segmentation competitions that combine volume normalization, first-stage organ localization, high-resolution 3D Swin-UNet or Swin Transformer UNet segmentation, boundary-refinement/Dice/Hausdorff losses, 3D elastic augmentation, spatio-temporal or multi-phase CT feature fusion, mixed-precision bf16 training, and post-processed 3D masks.
dejargonized_summary: Normalize a 3D medical scan, find the organ or anatomy first, crop a high-resolution region, segment the lesion or organ with a 3D UNet-style model, train with losses that care about boundaries and overlap, and clean the final mask for the medical metric.

inputs.name: medical_volumes
inputs.constraints: 3D CT/MRI volumes, spacing/orientation metadata, masks, patient IDs, and optional multi-phase studies.

outputs.name: segmentation_masks
outputs.constraints: 3D organ, lesion, or tumor masks formatted for Dice, Hausdorff, or challenge-specific scoring.

use_when: The task outputs 3D medical segmentation masks for organs, lesions, tumors, or subtle boundaries rather than only class labels.

Winning techniques include coarse-to-fine ROI localization, 3D Swin-UNet, Swin Transformer UNet, boundary-refinement loss, Dice/Hausdorff optimization, 3D elastic deformation, multi-phase or spatio-temporal CT fusion, mixed-precision bf16 training, or connected-component mask post-processing.
The hard part is localizing a small anatomy or lesion and preserving boundary quality in a high-resolution crop.
do_not_use_when: The target is only a patient-level class probability with no mask output.
The input is gigapixel histopathology tiles where stain normalization and tile stitching dominate.
The solution is natural image semantic segmentation with no 3D scan geometry or medical ROI localization.
applicability.key_insight: The durable topology is coarse organ localization followed by high-resolution 3D ROI segmentation and boundary-aware metric calibration. It differs from 3D medical classification because the output artifact is a spatial mask and boundary losses are load-bearing.

swappable_stages.coarse_roi_localization: Can use a low-resolution 3D model, organ detector, atlas crop, connected-component prior, or segmentation prepass.
swappable_stages.high_resolution_segmentation: Can use 3D Swin-UNet, nnU-Net, UNETR, V-Net, 3D U-Net, or Swin Transformer UNet backbones.
swappable_stages.boundary_metric_training: Can use Boundary-Refinement, Dice, Tversky, focal Dice, Hausdorff, surface distance, or hybrid segmentation losses.

applicability.scaling_notes: Precompute resampled volumes and coarse crops, keep normalization fold-local, and use mixed precision plus patch sampling to fit high-resolution 3D models.
failure_modes: A poor first-stage crop can exclude the lesion before the high-resolution model sees it.
Optimizing Dice alone can miss thin infiltrative boundaries that dominate Hausdorff distance.
Patient leakage through repeated studies or augmentation caches can inflate validation scores.

planning_constraints.subject: coarse_localization_before_high_resolution_segmentation
planning_constraints.statement: Run organ or anatomy localization before high-resolution lesion segmentation unless the full scan can be processed at target resolution.
planning_constraints.rationale: Small 3D lesions are hard to segment when the model's receptive field and memory budget are spent on irrelevant anatomy.

audit.rationale: Added after validation left 3D medical segmentation cases divergent and semantic comparison showed classification-focused RSNA CDGs and gigapixel histopathology segmentation CDGs did not capture coarse-to-fine 3D ROI masks, boundary-refinement losses, and Dice/Hausdorff output contracts.
audit.dejargonized_summary: This covers medical segmentation solutions where finding the organ first and preserving 3D lesion boundaries are the reusable structure.
uncertainty_notes: If a future case uses segmentation only as an auxiliary pretraining signal and outputs class probabilities, use the multiview classification CDG instead.

references.title: Sciona 135-CDG expansion validation audit
references.note: Local deterministic and semantic audit of unmatched 3D medical segmentation patterns.

stages.name: Volume Normalization
stages.description: Normalize orientation, spacing, intensity windows, contrast phases, and patient grouping for CT or MRI volumes before segmentation.
stages.dejargonized_description: Put all 3D scans into a comparable coordinate and intensity space.
preconditions: Spacing, orientation, and patient metadata are available.
guarantees: Volumes are aligned enough for ROI localization.

stages.name: Coarse ROI Localization
stages.description: Use a first-stage 3D model, organ detector, atlas crop, or low-resolution segmentation pass to localize the pancreas, organ, tumor neighborhood, or target anatomy.
stages.dejargonized_description: Find the organ or region before doing detailed segmentation.
preconditions: Coarse localization model or crop rule is selected.
guarantees: Target anatomy is retained in the high-resolution crop.

stages.name: High-Resolution Segmentation
stages.description: Train 3D Swin-UNet, Swin Transformer UNet, nnU-Net, UNETR, V-Net, or 3D U-Net models on ROI crops with patch sampling, 3D elastic deformation, and multi-phase or spatio-temporal feature fusion.
stages.dejargonized_description: Segment the organ or lesion in the focused high-resolution crop.
preconditions: Segmentation labels and patch sampling policy are fixed.
guarantees: Voxel predictions are produced for the target anatomy.

stages.name: Boundary Metric Training
stages.description: Optimize Boundary-Refinement, Dice, Tversky, focal Dice, Hausdorff, or surface-distance losses with mixed-precision bf16 training and fold ensembling.
stages.dejargonized_description: Train the model to get both overlap and lesion boundaries right.
preconditions: Metric and class weights are known.
guarantees: Mask probabilities are optimized for boundary-sensitive scoring.

stages.name: Mask Postprocessing
stages.description: Apply connected-component filtering, hole filling, anatomical constraints, threshold tuning, crop-to-volume reinsertion, and submission formatting for Dice/Hausdorff scoring.
stages.dejargonized_description: Clean the predicted mask and put it back into the original scan space.
preconditions: Original volume geometry and thresholds are available.
guarantees: Masks are valid in the challenge coordinate system.
